05 / 05

EV Charger
HMI Study

Team project with Manomay Upadhye, Raveen Kovil & Arnav Rajani — Human–Machine Interaction

A human–machine interaction study of residential EV chargers. We audited the Exicom Spin Air, which has only one LED strip and relies on a phone app for everything else, and redesigned its grip, feedback, safety lock and controls around a mechanical clunk and physical buttons.

Industrial DesignHMIErgonomicsEV Charging
ChargerResidential AC wall unit, Type 2 plug
GripSized for 50th percentile female to 95th percentile male hands
FeedbackMechanical clunk, LED ring, screen and haptic click
SafetyActive lock while current is flowing
Final prototype
Journey
ResearchCharging became a habit; users trust the car dashboard over the charger
EvaluationAudited Type 2 and DC chargers; cognitive load measured with NASA-TLX
DesignLayered feedback, on-device errors, safety lock, UPI payment, tactile controls
PrototypeHousing form tested in CAD, mockups and a final prototype
Ideation & process
